12 September 2026 · Local refinement report

Paper now has a coherent page structure

All eleven primary designs and six supporting routes received a critical refinement pass. The shared frame now aligns, rankings appear substantially earlier, forms follow a clear sequence, and reading records have a consistent hierarchy.

The work keeps Tadoku’s Paper identity—warm canvas, serif headings and violet actions—and improves how those elements work together. Page owners and a separate reviewer inspected the application in the browser and corrected issues found in the combined result.

Delivery: logical local commits on t3code/paper-visual-refinement. No push or pull request. The sample application remains unpublished.

The leaderboard carries the page

The previous page placed several disconnected introductions, controls and explanations ahead of the rankings. Round context, filters, personal position, table and pagination now form one working sheet; supporting information sits alongside it.

Readable controls take priority

Language and activity selections occupy separate rows on narrow screens. The selected values remain readable, the personal standing stays attached to the table, and “Find my row” still moves to and focuses the correct participant.

The additional mobile review also brought the admin’s first Review action into the 390 × 844 viewport and moved the log score preview above Save.

What real pages fixed in Paper

  • One application frame. Header, content and footer use the same 1160px maximum content area and responsive gutters. Nested prose and form columns retain that alignment.
  • Fields follow their parent. Removed the field component’s fixed 32rem maximum; full-width inputs now align with paired rows and can shrink inside a grid.
  • Stable autocomplete controls. Dropdown triggers stay at the inline edge with 44 × 44px targets. Long selected labels wrap without colliding with their remove action or the trigger.
  • Recognizable account navigation. ActionMenu supports a decorative custom trigger icon; the mobile account uses a person icon. Account and Navbar menu buttons remain 44 × 44px at comfortable and compact density.
  • Correct responsive calendar tooltips. SVG tooltip backgrounds now use getBBox() rather than CSS-pixel measurements. In the real scaled calendar, the background now matches the text plus its intended padding: 179.90 SVG units, down from the incorrect 260.55.
  • Score before saving. The activity form keeps one visible personal-score summary: beside the form on desktop, before Save on mobile.

The styleguide now explains shared page gutters and parent-controlled form widths, demonstrates a full-width title with paired amount/date fields, and documents the custom account-menu icon. Final browser checks confirmed the rendered examples, their visible guidance and the 44 × 44px account trigger.

Validation and limits

389 automated checks passed: 204 Paper tests, 141 styleguide tests, 41 playground tests and 3 boundary tests. Typechecks, lint and relevant builds passed, along with 49 example typechecks, the TypeScript 4.9 consumer check, package packing checks and import-boundary checks.

Browser review covered desktop and mobile compositions, with 320, 390, 768 and 1280px checks and representative dark/compact states. The shared-frame sweep checked 15 routes at 320 and 768px: all 30 observations had aligned edges, no unintended page overflow and no broken images.

Interaction checks included filtering and search recovery, finding a leaderboard row, FAQ disclosures, account-menu keyboard focus, invalid log amounts, settings saves, local contact drafts, submission eligibility and editor/dialog dismissal. The new tooltip regressions failed before the fix and passed afterward.

The remaining tooling output is advisory: eight existing playground Fast Refresh warnings, one existing styleguide compiler warning, and bundle-size advisories. Passing tests support behavior and geometry; the screenshots and peer review support the visual conclusions.

No blocking visual decisions were deferred. This remains a sample data playground, ready for review in its private preview. Backend integration and real participant content remain separate application work.
